anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Replication Synchronization Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-layer statement or transaction design forces the engine to process, scan, or return more data and to hold locks longer than functionally required.
Replication Synchronization Anomaly : Downstream replicas or subscribers cannot receive or apply primary WAL/redo at production rate, leading to growing replication lag and log-retention pressure on the primary.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : The transport and connection-handling path between clients and the database is saturated or unstable, throttling session establishment and data transfer.

When all three anomalies occur together the system experiences an acute mix of long-running, data-heavy transactions, widening replica apply delay, and deteriorating client connectivity. Clients observe erratic response times, frequent timeouts both during query execution and connection setup, stale reads from lagging replicas, mounting numbers of aborted or retried transactions, and explosive growth of primary-side WAL or binlog storage. Monitoring shows bloated slow-query logs, replication delay graphs climbing in parallel with network retransmission rates, ballooning counts of idle-in-transaction or client-read waits, and listener backlogs filling while replicas fall further behind.

Causally, chatty or data-intensive workload logic inflates result sets and transaction sizes, increasing primary log volume. The surge of log traffic must traverse the same constrained network links that already struggle to serve front-end clients; packet loss or bandwidth saturation slows both client I/O and replica streaming. As replicas slip, the primary is forced to retain additional log segments, further stressing local storage and lengthening checkpoints. In turn, the extended transaction durations caused by sub-optimal SQL keep locks and snapshots open longer, amplifying replica apply contention and prolonging network socket occupancy. The intertwined effects create a feedback loop where poor workload design generates excess data, congested networks delay its delivery, and replication lag feeds back into longer client wait times and heavier retry storms, collectively degrading overall database performance and availability.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for more data from a source/replica connection before aborting the read.
entry.trigger_condition: A replica waits longer than replica_net_timeout for more data from the source connection.
entry.workload_impact: The replication network read is aborted and the replica considers the connection interrupted.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL replication system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
